http://www.reaxxion.com/10195/why-star-citizen-is-likely-going-to-be-a-complete-disaster Summary: Derek Smart states why he is skeptical about the star citizen game.

I had not been paying attention to star citizen, and as such what caught my attention was this:

so they are making concept art for ships, some were actual models, and then selling them at a premium. People keep buying them. This, despite the fact that there is still no “game” to play them with. In short, the result is that you have ships you’ve bought, with no game to play them with.

This is something that we should monitor. It affects gamergate in a few subtle ways: Its about a game, its about a game that had been hyped up, and this hype led to a lot of consumer money thrown at it.

85 million dollars, is a lot of money. Something must be shown for it. If the game that comes out of it, does not meet reasonable expectations for that amount of money, then regulators WILL get involved.

If that happens, buy popcorn, cause it will be one hell of a shitstorm.

US law is set on precedence. the FTC is taking kickstarter seriously. Considering how new crowdfunding is, this is a very quick response by the regulatory agency.

As such, with events being what they are, and things turning out they way that they are. I believe that new actions are available to us.

What this means, is that we may see some results if we were to write our politicians, and explain why we are upset at the games journalist publications. If we can demonstrate: a coherent money trail, plausible conflict of interests, and show the misinformation that some of the publications have done, this may be enough to cause authorities to take an interest, and start investigating.

We have a lot of information already on deep freeze. And more keeps coming to light.

Keep in mind, that this is very much a consumer revolt. this has been 10 years in the making. Too many people have been burned by bad purchases, biased industry reporting, and shitty business practices. As such, people on the outside that deal with businesses, see gamergate as a consumer dispute. They simply do not get involved, because it does not affect them, yet.
